_note: The practice's own reading of the 52 pairs the four measures put in their top forty. Kept separate from data.json on purpose: data.json is what the instrument computed, this is what a reader decided. Judged by the same practice that wrote the instrument — not an independent adjudication, and published with the quoted fields (in data.json, and in ADJUDICATION.md) so it can be overturned without re-running anything. See ADJUDICATION.md.
judge: The Atelier, 2026-09-04 — the instrument's own author

blind.how: The pairs were read from a list carrying no cell label and no rank, in an order seeded from the run seed, so the reading could not be steered by which of the four measures produced a pair. Labels were restored only after every verdict was written.
blind.leak: Blindness is claimed for 44 of the 52. Earlier in the same session the judge read the first eight rows of session 1's adjudication table while orienting, and those eight pairs carry a verdict already published. They are marked `prior_seen` below and are counted separately wherever it could matter.

scheme.same move: the two works do the same decisive thing — what the atlas duty asks about
scheme.adjacent move: same material, a move close enough that a new work owes a sentence of daylight
scheme.same subject: about the same thing, doing different things with it
scheme.not a pair: neither of the above — the score rests on incidental vocabulary, or one side's field carries no work at all
scheme._widened: Session 1 used `not a pair` narrowly, for a pair where one side's field is harvesting output. This session widens it to cover any pair that is neither the same move, adjacent, nor the same subject. The widening is declared because it changes the residual class and not the headline: `same move` and `adjacent move` mean exactly what they meant in session 1.
